question.text: Will Levent Alpöge and Ethan Sussman publicly post a manuscript proving four-dimensional Yang–Mills existence by November 13, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, by November 13, 2026, 23:59 UTC, a manuscript authored by Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) and Ethan Sussman (Northwestern University) that asserts a proof of the existence of four-dimensional pure Yang–Mills theory is publicly accessible as either (i) an arXiv preprint, in any category, listing both as authors (other co-authors permitted), or (ii) a standalone paper-style document on a personal or institutional web page of either author (for example https://ethanwsussman.github.io/, a northwestern.edu page, or an anthropic.com page) with a title, an author list naming both, and an abstract or introduction stating such a theorem. It resolves NO if no such manuscript is publicly accessible by that deadline. Files in code repositories, READMEs, notes, talk slides, social-media posts and news reports do not qualify. Resolution is checked against the arXiv author listings for Alpöge (https://arxiv.org/search/?searchtype=author&query=Alpoge) and Sussman (https://arxiv.org/search/?searchtype=author&query=Sussman%2C+E) and Sussman's website (https://ethanwsussman.github.io/); if those are unavailable or inconclusive, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) apply.
question.fine_print: A construction of four-dimensional pure Yang–Mills theory for SU(2) alone suffices; a document that only treats lower-dimensional or finite-volume settings, or only the mass gap, does not qualify. Whether the document labels itself a draft or preprint, or states that its content is unvetted or LLM-assisted, does not affect resolution. "Publicly accessible" means viewable without registration, payment, or an invitation. The relevant date is when the manuscript first became publicly viewable (the arXiv submission date shown on the abstract page, or the posting date on the web page), not a later revision or a subsequent public announcement about the work.

research:
I've checked every resolution source, the repository and the press coverage. As of November 3, 2026, nothing that would resolve this YES has been posted, and the authors' own README says they are rewriting the four-dimensional proof slowly rather than rushing it out.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: Sussman's arXiv author listing has 19 entries. The newest is "The asymptotic structure of forward scattering" (27 Aug 2026). Nothing on Yang-Mills. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/search/?searchtype=author&query=Sussman%2C+E)
- 2026-11-03: Alpöge's arXiv listing has 22 entries. The newest is the IPM blow-up paper with Buckmaster and Coiculescu (14 Sep 2026). Nothing on gauge theory. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/search/?searchtype=author&query=Alpoge)
- 2026-11-03: Sussman's website lists 16 papers, the newest being arXiv:2608.27815. Its only Yang-Mills mention is a "[LINK]" to the GitHub repository under "Quantum field theory". There is no manuscript. [ethanwsussman.github.io](https://ethanwsussman.github.io/)

## 2. Current status
- The question is not settled. No paper-style manuscript qualifies yet.
- 2026-11-01: A commit to the GitHub repository, "Update YM4 proof sketch and add matching 505-page PDF", added a four-dimensional proof sketch. The question's rules exclude files in code repositories, so this does not count unless it is moved to arXiv or a personal or institutional page. [GitHub commits](https://github.com/ethanwsussman/Yang--Mills-LLM-experiment/commits/main)
- The current README (undated "Update", around Oct 31) says:
  - YM4 is "unfinished": about 61k pages of total "slop", of which about 20k pages are "closed (refereed and frozen)".
  - They are rewriting it "much more methodically (thus quite slowly!)", and will first demonstrate the key arguments in the simpler QED3 and YM3 settings.
  - They explicitly reject rushing out a "10,000-page slop".
  - They want a collaborative rewrite at a "human pace", with credit shared the way experimental physics collaborations do it.
  - They say they are "not stuck" and that an open alternative to OpenAI is now more important.
  - The README mentions no arXiv plans or timeline. [README](https://github.com/ethanwsussman/Yang--Mills-LLM-experiment)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: The repository is being actively edited: a new YM3_main manuscript, revised QCD3 proofs, and a refreshed QED3 manuscript (242 pages). Effort is going into the three-dimensional write-ups. [commits](https://github.com/ethanwsussman/Yang--Mills-LLM-experiment/commits/main)
- 2026-11-02: Sam Altman said OpenAI's next-generation GPT will be released "soon" (news API, ifeng). Peter Woit's blog criticised the KITP conference organised by OpenAI-affiliated physicists, and calls the Sussman-Alpöge 4D work "tens of thousands of pages of unchecked slop". [Woit](https://www.math.columbia.edu/~woit/wordpress/)
- 2026-10-31: A README update and a merged pull request from an outside contributor (FireflySentinel). [commits](https://github.com/ethanwsussman/Yang--Mills-LLM-experiment/commits/main)
- 2026-10-27: Scientific American ("Dueling proofs") reports the pair "believed they were close to finishing". It gives no publication plans and notes OpenAI's paper is also unreleased. [SciAm](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/dueling-proofs-from-openai-and-anthropic-astound-scientists/)
- 2026-10-27: In a separate Scientific American piece, Sussman says "we were on the way and maybe even as close as a few weeks away". [SciAm](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/openai-just-scooped-human-researchers-on-a-million-dollar-quantum-math-problem/); [quantumresearch.center](https://quantumresearch.center/news/articles/openai-yang-mills-existence/)
- Third parties have posted related material on GitHub: Aronow and Lopatto on YM3 on the torus, and miaomiao77's checks. None of it is by the pair. [pmaronow](https://github.com/pmaronow/3d-ym-torus); [miaomiao77](https://github.com/miaomiao77/Yang--Mills-LLM-experiment)

## 4. Base rates
- In the four weeks since the repository went public on October 6, the pair has put all their Yang-Mills material on GitHub and posted none of it to arXiv, including the more polished QED3 and YM3 manuscripts. The 153-page "zeroth draft" has not been turned into a preprint either.
- Both authors do post regularly on arXiv: Alpöge three times between August and September 2026, Sussman about two to four times a year. None of those papers concern this project.
- There is a precedent for posting fast: Anthropic's ETH paper and Lean proof went up within a day of OpenAI's October 26 announcement. But that was an official Anthropic release, not this personal side project.
- I found no clear precedent for a two-week turnaround from an unreadable, tens-of-thousands-page draft to an arXiv-ready 4D manuscript.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, "When will Yang-Mills and the Mass Gap be resolved?": 0.11 before 2027, 0.21 before 2028. This market concerns the full Clay problem including the mass gap, so it does not match this question.
- Kalshi, "Which Millennium Prize Problem will be solved next?": Yang-Mills at 0.43. Only loosely related.
- I found no Manifold, Polymarket or Metaculus market on an Alpöge-Sussman posting.

## 6. Upcoming events before November 13
- OpenAI's physics write-up with David Gross's group could be released. That might push the pair to post a priority claim, for example by moving the 505-page YM4 sketch to arXiv. The stated "human pace" plan argues against it.
- Repository activity is daily. Watch for the YM4 sketch being relabelled as a manuscript and posted on arXiv or Sussman's site, and for any new README note.
- A new arXiv submission would show up in listings about one business day after it is sent. A submission made before November 13 could still appear just after the deadline, but what counts is the submission date shown on the abstract page.

The pair's GitHub repository is very active, but its newest four-dimensional file is a 505-page "proof sketch", and repository files don't count under the criteria. The README says the four-dimensional write-up is going "much more methodically (thus quite slowly!)" and warns against rushing out "10,000-page slop".

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03 (checked): Sussman's arXiv listing has 19 results. The newest is "The asymptotic structure of forward scattering" (Lohr, Oltman, Sussman, Zou), arXiv:2608.27815, 27 Aug 2026. Nothing is on gauge theory. [arXiv Sussman](https://arxiv.org/search/?searchtype=author&query=Sussman%2C+E)
- 2026-11-03 (checked): Alpöge's listing has 22 results. The newest is the IPM blow-up paper with Buckmaster and Coiculescu, 14 Sep 2026. Nothing is on Yang-Mills. [arXiv Alpoge](https://arxiv.org/search/?searchtype=author&query=Alpoge)
- 2026-11-03 (checked): Sussman's website lists 16 papers, the newest being arXiv:2608.27815. Yang-Mills appears only under "Current topics of interest", as a "[LINK]" to the GitHub repository. There is no Yang-Mills preprint. [ethanwsussman.github.io](https://ethanwsussman.github.io/)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. No qualifying arXiv or web-page manuscript exists as of 2026-11-03.
- 2026-11-01: a commit titled "Update YM4 proof sketch and add matching 505-page PDF" was made. Earlier, on 2026-10-31, the four-dimensional file YM4M1 was renamed "YM4_sketch_draft". These are repository files and do not qualify. [commits](https://github.com/ethanwsussman/Yang--Mills-LLM-experiment/commits/main)
- The README describes the state of the four-dimensional work as follows. [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanwsussman/Yang--Mills-LLM-experiment/main/README.md)

  - The planned order is QED3, then YM3, then YM4.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: commits were mostly three-dimensional work: "Add YM3_main manuscript and TeX source", revised QCD3 proofs and a refreshed QED3 manuscript. The repository has 85 commits, and activity is heavy from Oct 26 to Nov 2. [commits](https://github.com/ethanwsussman/Yang--Mills-LLM-experiment/commits/main)

This also comes from the collected news item. [infobae](https://www.infobae.com/tecno/2026/11/02/matematicos-temen-que-openai-y-anthropic-controlen-quien-accede-a-los-hallazgos-de-sus-ia/)

- 2026-10-27: Scientific American's "Dueling proofs" article says the pair "believed they were near to finishing the program". It mentions no preprint by them, only the GitHub repository. [SciAm](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/dueling-proofs-from-openai-and-anthropic-astound-scientists/)
- 2026-10-26: Peter Woit's post "Secret Unified Physics Slop" calls the four-dimensional claim "tens of thousands of pages of unchecked slop". [Woit](https://www.math.columbia.edu/~woit/wordpress/?p=15948)
  - Sussman commented there that the three-dimensional draft is "presentable (albeit still unpolished)". He said its claim is convergence along a subsequence, with the OS axioms claimed.
  - Another commenter said the posted work covers only a limited class of gauge-invariant observables.
- Late Oct 2026 (exact date not checked): Alpöge posted on X that Sussman "has been writing up existence of YM4 publicly via Balaban's approach". He described the repository as holding QED3, YM3 and "an old preliminary outline of YM4". [X](https://x.com/__alpoge__/status/2114838067953770981)

### 4. Base rates
- I found no direct base rate. Both authors post on arXiv regularly, roughly several papers a year each, but neither has ever posted Yang-Mills or LLM-generated constructive QFT work there.
- In the four weeks since the repository went public (Oct 6), they have put manuscript material in the repository instead of on arXiv. This holds even for the three-dimensional drafts, which Sussman calls presentable, so the four-dimensional draft, which they call unreadable, seems even less likely to reach arXiv first.
- Historically, Balaban-style constructions have taken years to write up. The README's stated QED3, then YM3, then YM4 order points to the four-dimensional paper coming after the three-dimensional papers.
- Possible complication: arXiv moderation of very long LLM-written mathematics could delay or block a submission. This is my own inference; I did not verify arXiv policy.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market on this specific question on Manifold, Polymarket or Kalshi.
- Kalshi, "When will Yang-Mills and the Mass Gap be resolved?": Before 2027 at 0.11, Before 2028 at 0.21. This needs the full Clay problem, including the mass gap, so it does not match this question.
- Kalshi, "Which Millennium Prize Problem will be solved next?": Yang-Mills at 0.43. This is only loosely related.

### 6. Upcoming events before Nov 13
- The repository is being updated daily. Possible next steps include turning "YM4_sketch_draft" or the assembly overview into a full manuscript, or posting the three-dimensional manuscripts to arXiv. Three-dimensional papers would not count.
- A posting cut-off note: arXiv shows the date of submission. Submissions before about 14:00 ET on weekdays are announced the next weekday. Posting directly to Sussman's website would avoid that delay. This timing is my inference.
- OpenAI may release its paper with the group led by David Gross, or the next-generation GPT Altman mentioned. Either could add priority pressure or prompt a rapid response.
- Watch for further posts by Alpöge on X about priority.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) There are about 10 days left, until November 13, 2026, 23:59 UTC. For Yes, a paper-style manuscript by both Alpöge and Sussman asserting existence of 4D (SU(2)) Yang-Mills must become publicly viewable, either on arXiv or as a standalone paper on one of their personal or institutional pages. Files in the GitHub repository do not count.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. As of November 3 there is no qualifying arXiv posting or web-page manuscript. The 4D material exists only as GitHub repository files.

(c) Base rate: researchers who have publicly described a draft as "extremely long and basically not understandable" rarely produce a readable, paper-style posting within a two-week window. Even under priority pressure, I would put this at roughly 5-10%. The pair's own behaviour fits that. In four weeks they have posted none of their Yang-Mills material, not even the more polished QED3 and YM3 write-ups, to arXiv.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - On October 27, Sussman said they were "maybe even as close as a few weeks away."
  - Priority pressure from OpenAI's October 26 announcement is real.
  - A 505-page YM4 proof sketch was added to the repository on November 1, and it could be moved to Sussman's site quickly.
  - Anthropic has shown it can post fast (the ETH paper went up October 27).
- For No:
  - The README update around October 31 says YM4 is "unfinished."
  - It says they are rewriting it "methodically (thus quite slowly!)," starting with QED3 and YM3, and want a collaborative rewrite at a "human pace."
  - It explicitly rejects rushing out "10,000-page slop" and mentions no arXiv plans.
  - Activity on November 2 focused on the 3D manuscripts.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: they keep polishing QED3 and YM3 in the repository, and the YM4 sketch stays a GitHub file through November 13.
- Yes: OpenAI and the Gross group release their paper, and the pair responds by posting the 505-page YM4 sketch to arXiv as a priority claim, with a title, authors and an abstract stating the theorem.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 7%. I move down because the authors have explicitly said they will not rush a 4D posting and are working on the lower-dimensional cases first. I keep some probability for a priority-driven reversal, since a 505-page sketch exists and a triggering OpenAI release is plausible. I land at about 4%.
